parts:
Hi Mike,
Here is my code including the extent I download and extract the data by micro_era5, I tried the "write_input=1", but it didn't work.
The timed out just happen in some coordinates, below is an example

  #bounding coordinates (in WGS84 / EPSG:4326)
  xmn<- 80
  xmx<- 110
  ymn<- 25
  ymx<- 45
 
  #temporal extent
  st_time<-lubridate::ymd("1985:03:01")
  en_time<-lubridate::ymd("1985:10:31")

  # filename and location for downloaded .nc files
  file_prefix<-"Era5_QT"
  op <-"/Users/jiangzhongwen/Desktop/2021/QT/Zhong-wen/Data"
 
  # build a request (covering multiple years)
  req<-build_era5_request(xmin = xmn, xmax = xmx,
                          ymin = ymn, ymax = ymx,
                          start_time = st_time,
                          end_time = en_time,
                          outfile_name = file_prefix)
 
  # Obtaining data with a request
  request_era5(request = req, uid = uid, out_path = op)




####extract the data by micro_era5

dstart=paste("01/03/",1985,spe="")
dfinish=paste("31/10/",1985,sep="")
lon=95.25000
lat=39.58333

micro<-micro_era5(
  write_input = 1,
  run.gads = 2,
  loc=c(lon,lat), 
  dstart=dstart, 
  dfinish=dfinish, 
  REFL=0.35, 
  Usrhyt=1.5,  
  runshade=1, 
  warm=0, 
  spatial="/Users/jiangzhongwen/Desktop/2021/QT/Zhong-wen/Data/Era5_QT", 
  RUF=0.0003, 
  CMH2O=0.5, 
  rainoff=0 
)




All the best,

Zhong-wen

parts:
Hi Mike and Zhong-wen,

I tried this on my end just to see if this may be an issue with the mcera5 package, which supplies the ERA5 data for micro_era5() and I maintain. Zhong-wen I can confirm that the same issue you have found is occurring on my end– the model hangs when provided certain coordinates, but runs successfully for others. I'm not finding issues with the underlying ERA5 data so far, and extraction from the netCDF via mcera5 seems to be fine– but I'll keep tabs on this Mike.

Best,
Dave

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: micro_era5 issue
parts:
Hi Zhong-wen (and Dave),

I tried it too and had the same problem. The main thing is that it starts off under very cold conditions with a large rainfall event, which is hard for the integrator in terms of the snow calculation (it works fine with the snow model turned off). So you can either start it in summer (best solution), or increase the ERR parameter (I got it to complete with ERR = 5).

Note also that your code for specifying the dates puts a space before the year:

which does cause a problem when the R code uses those dates to get the number of years (I need an error trap for this input). Instead use:

dstart=paste0("01/03/",1985)
dfinish=paste0("31/10/",1985).

All the best,
Mike
